sites.quote: Note that the resolver must always be guided by local policy when deciding whether to authenticate a new public key, even if the local policy is simply to authenticate any new public key for which the resolver is able verify the signature.
sites.reason: RFC 4033 is the introduction to the DNSSEC set and uses no RFC 2119 keyword; this lowercase 'must' introduces an obligation on zone signers, validating resolvers or zone transfer that RFC 4034 and RFC 4035 state with RFC 2119 keywords.

sites.quote: Note that the private keys used to sign zone data must be kept secure and should be stored offline when practical.

sites.quote: Security-aware resolvers authenticate zone information by forming an authentication chain from a newly learned public key back to a previously known authentication public key, which in turn either has been configured into the resolver or must have been learned and verified previously.
sites.reason: RFC 4033 is the introduction to the DNSSEC set and uses no RFC 2119 keyword; this lowercase 'must' introduces an obligation on zone signers, validating resolvers or zone transfer that RFC 4034 and RFC 4035 state with RFC 2119 keywords.

sites.quote: Therefore, the resolver must be configured with at least one trust anchor.

sites.quote: Security-aware resolvers must also be capable of forming an authentication chain from a newly learned zone back to an authentication key, as described above.
sites.reason: RFC 4033 is the introduction to the DNSSEC set and uses no RFC 2119 keyword; this lowercase 'must' introduces an obligation on zone signers, validating resolvers or zone transfer that RFC 4034 and RFC 4035 state with RFC 2119 keywords.

sites.quote: If a security-aware resolver must rely on an unsigned zone or a name server that is not security aware, the resolver may not be able to validate DNS responses and will need a local policy on whether to accept unverified responses.
sites.reason: Describes the situation in which a resolver must rely on an unsigned zone; the lowercase 'must' is conditional narration, and the consequence is stated as 'will need a local policy'.

sites.quote: Although not strictly required to do so by the protocol, most DNS queries originate from stub resolvers.
sites.reason: Descriptive statement that most queries come from stub resolvers; it says the protocol does not require it and obliges nobody.

sites.quote: Even a security-oblivious stub resolver may benefit from DNSSEC if the recursive name servers it uses are security-aware, but for the stub resolver to place any real reliance on DNSSEC services, the stub resolver must trust both the recursive name servers in question and the communication channels between itself and those name servers.
sites.reason: Introduces the stub-resolver trust obligation, which RFC 4035 Section 4.9.3 states with RFC 2119 keywords (RFC4035-4.9.3-2).

sites.quote: Because inclusion of these DNSSEC RRs could easily cause UDP message truncation and fallback to TCP, a security-aware name server must also support the EDNS "sender's UDP payload" mechanism.
sites.reason: Introduces the EDNS0 payload-size obligation of a security-aware name server, which RFC 4035 Section 3 states with RFC 2119 keywords as RFC4035-3-1 and RFC4035-3-2.

sites.quote: In order for a security-aware resolver to validate a DNS response, all zones along the path from the trusted starting point to the zone containing the response zones must be signed, and all name servers and resolvers involved in the resolution process must be security-aware, as defined in this document set.
